description: Figure 19 is a grouped vertical bar chart illustrating the average probing accuracy using different MLP variations, with hidden layer sizes indicated in square brackets. The horizontal axis displays four categorical MLP variations arranged from left to right: "hidden:[50], linear", "hidden:[], linear", "hidden:[100], ReLU", and "hidden:[50, 50], ReLU". The vertical value axis is labeled "% point difference" and uses a linear scale ranging from -0.2 to 0.2, with tick marks and corresponding horizontal grid lines at intervals of 0.1. The chart features grouped bars, where each category on the horizontal axis contains a pair of side-by-side bars representing two models, as defined by the legend in the top right: "mBERT" in light blue on the left and "XLM-R" in dark blue on the right. The bar values extend both above and below the 0.0 baseline. The lowest value is observed for the mBERT model in the "hidden:[50], linear" category at approximately -0.18, while the highest value is seen for the XLM-R model in the "hidden:[], linear" category at 0.2. Other approximate values include -0.05 for XLM-R in the first category, 0.09 for mBERT in the second category, -0.09 and 0.02 for mBERT and XLM-R respectively in the "hidden:[100], ReLU" category, and -0.14 and -0.12 for mBERT and XLM-R in the "hidden:[50, 50], ReLU" category. The categories are not sorted in a strictly ascending, descending, or alphabetical order, and no specific bars are visually emphasized with additional annotations or distinct outlines.
